items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: And Louis came in and spoke to me and told me how he thought I sounded, and said keep it up and you’re doing fine and all like that.

ctx.x: What a marvelous man he was.

Oh he really was. You know when I was with Billy in the 50s, he was playing with Louis Armstrong, and Billy and I were playing opposite them. And Milt got hung up at a record date. And as a kid, I started, I was playing, maybe I was about fourteen years old. And I shouldn’t have been but I was playing in a trio in a nightclub in the Bronx. And Louis came in and spoke to me and told me how he thought I sounded, and said keep it up and you’re doing fine and all like that. And he knew I was a bass player with…
I notice you started playing some electric bass.
